correctness.rationale: For compactly supported positive pole measures, the window is in L² and its negative-frequency Fourier representation yields an absolutely convergent critical Zak formula. The exact cross kernel is positive and, by a partial-fraction identity with derivative q(1−q²)/D_q², strictly increasing in cos θ; positive exponential coefficients increase with the frequency coordinate. Hence the sharp essential minimum and maximum are at the two boundary corners, yielding exactly the stated A and B. Their square-root ratio is a positive weighted average of R(R+1)/(R−1), whose unique minimum is 3+2√2. Equality requires a single point mass at R=1+√2. The script checked 79024 supplementary finite exact/numerical assertions; the analytic argument, not the checks, proves the universal quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The closest primary results establish (i) qualitative Gabor-frame existence for finite positive-pole Herglotz windows and the general Zak-type function (Belov–Kulikov–Lyubarskii 2021), and (ii) sharp constants for a single Cauchy pole (Belov–Kulikov–Lyubarskii 2022). The new quantified result establishes simultaneous monotonicity of the squared Zak transform for arbitrary positive finite or continuous pole mixtures, computes both optimal bounds from two explicit positive integrals, and solves the global best-conditioning problem over all such mixtures with a unique extremizer and constant 17+12√2. The older one-pole constant is explicitly credited. A general Zak representation enables but does not itself state or directly optimize these quantitative invariants.

value.rationale: Critical-density Gabor stability is measured by the optimal frame bounds and their condition ratio. The existing qualitative maximal-frame-set theorem leaves these natural invariants undetermined for multi-pole windows. The new two-variable positivity mechanism gives complete sharp constants for all positive finite or continuous pole mixtures and a universal dimensionless conditioning barrier, including the unique best window. It answers a natural design question—whether positive mixing can improve conditioning—rather than evaluating an arbitrary numerical example or restating frame existence.
